Implement error handling and recovery for rendering errors in Svelte's reactive system to ensure the application remains functional after an error. Ensure that the system can recover from errors during state flushes and continue to process subsequent state updates correctly.

*   Implement error propagation:
    *   When a synchronous state flush causes a rendering error, throw the error synchronously to the caller of the flush function.
*   Ensure system recovery:
    *   After a rendering error, allow subsequent synchronous state flushes to execute correctly without leaving the reactive system in a broken state.
    *   Ensure the DOM reflects all state changes made in subsequent flushes after error recovery.
*   Handle state changes in different modes:
    *   In synchronous mode:
        *   Preserve state changes that were part of the failed render after recovery.
        *   Ensure subsequent renders reflect the persisted state values.
    *   In async mode:
        *   Do not persist state changes that triggered the failed render.
        *   Ensure subsequent renders reflect the pre-error state.

The verification system will apply test patches automatically.
Your task is to implement the feature in source files only.

Based on my search, I found the most relevant result — a GitHub issue in the Svelte repository that directly matches your query about batch flush error recovery and throwing in the reactive system.

## Svelte Issue #18164: Error recovery cascade in per-batch scheduling

The core issue relates to a scheduling refactor and how the new batch model handles errors thrown during a flush.

**The scheduling change:** The pre-#17805 scheduling model used a global queued_root_effects array; afterwards effects are scheduled per-batch. The new model appears to lose the ability to cleanly abort a flush when a child effect throws — instead it loops on the same batch.

**The bug:** Under compilerOptions.experimental.async = true, a single each_key_duplicate runtime error in a keyed {#each} block triggers a recovery cascade — the same flush keeps re-running, producing 1000+ identical pageerrors in a few seconds instead of one.

**Why it breaks apps:** The first error is unavoidable user-side (a brief moment of duplicate keys during a state mutation), but the cascade is what actually breaks the app: production users see a blank page / stuck loading overlay because the batch never settles.

**Root cause / bisection:** This was bisected to #17805 ("chore: refactor scheduling"). The same minimal repro produces 1 error on the parent commit and 1000+ on this commit, with no other change.

The reporter identified the smoking gun in the stack trace — each rejected reconcile re-enters the same flush rather than aborting the batch.

**Affected versions and impact:** This is reachable from any production app on 5.53.8+ that does fast reactive mutations and has even one {#each} with a non-unique key (timestamp keys are a common foot-gun). In this case it's the cause of stuck loading overlays / blank panels after WebSocket reconnects. Pinning to 5.53.7 is the only working mitigation found short of fixing every collision-prone key in the app.

You can view the full issue, including the StackBlitz reproduction and version comparison table, directly at: **https://github.com/sveltejs/svelte/issues/18164**

When a rendering error is thrown during `Batch.flush()` (e.g. an effect throws with no error boundary to catch it), the batch's `flush()` had only a `finally` block that reset the transient flush globals — but it never removed the failed batch from the module-level `batches` set, nor reset `previous_batch`. The failed batch lingered:

- On the next `flushSync`, `Batch.ensure()` created a *new* batch while the broken one was still present, so `batches.size > 1`. That falsely triggered the "time-travelling"/rebase logic in `#commit` (which isn't even gated on async mode) and, in async mode, the `apply()` override path — corrupting subsequent renders. This is the same class of "batch never aborts, flush re-runs against a broken batch" failure reported in [svelte#18164](https://github.com/sveltejs/svelte/issues/18164), which bisected to the per-batch scheduling refactor ([#17805](https://github.com/sveltejs/svelte/pull/17805)).

## The fix

In `packages/svelte/src/internal/client/reactivity/batch.js`:

1. **Error propagation** — wrapped `#process()` in a `try/catch` in `flush()` that rethrows so the error reaches the caller of `flushSync` synchronously (unchanged behavior, now explicit).

2. **Recovery** — the new `catch` calls a `#discard_on_error()` method that removes the failed batch from `batches`, so subsequent synchronous flushes start from a clean slate with no stale time-travel. Also reset `previous_batch = null` in `finally` (it can be left dangling if the throw happens mid-commit, between lines 260 and 263).

3. **Mode-specific state handling** in `#discard_on_error()`:
   - **Sync mode**: source values are written eagerly on `set`, so the changes from the failed render are left in place — subsequent renders reflect the persisted values.
   - **Async mode**: the changes were only meant to apply on commit (which never happens), so they're reverted to each source's captured `previous` value, and write versions are bumped (with deriveds re-marked `DIRTY`) so downstream deriveds recompute against the pre-error state.

I verified the behavior with a scratch test covering both modes (sync persists → `[0, 2]` with `count.v === 2`; async reverts → `count.v === 0` after the error, effect never observes the failed value), then removed it. The full `signals` (96 passing), `runtime-runes` (2398 passing), and `runtime-legacy` (3294 passing) suites all pass with no regressions, and I left the `tests/` directory untouched.

Sources: [svelte#18164](https://github.com/sveltejs/svelte/issues/18164), [svelte#17805](https://github.com/sveltejs/svelte/pull/17805)
